body.heading: Start embarrassingly small
paragraphs: The biggest obstacle to volunteering is imagining it requires a transformed life. It requires a Tuesday. Food banks, libraries, park clean-ups, charity shops, and school clubs all run on people who give two ordinary hours, repeatedly. Pick the cause nearest your house or your heart — proximity beats passion for attendance.
One shift teaches you more about whether a role fits than a month of thinking about it.

body.heading: Be boringly reliable
paragraphs: Organisations do not need heroes; they need the person who actually arrives. The volunteer who comes every week, on time, and does the unglamorous task without being chased is worth more than a dozen enthusiastic maybes.
Reliability is also how trust — and the more interesting tasks — find you.

body.heading: Bring a friend, keep the debrief
paragraphs: Volunteering with a friend halves the awkwardness of the first day and doubles the chance you both return. Afterwards, over tea, compare notes: what surprised you, who you met, what you would do differently. The debrief is where service turns into understanding.
And if the first placement is wrong, change it without guilt. The right fit is not a luxury; it is what makes the habit survive the year.

takeaway: Take one small shift, be boringly reliable, and let the habit — not the heroics — do the work.
